interactive_questions.title: Cooperative Multitasking & Event Loop Scheduler
interactive_questions.question: Explore how Python's cooperative multitasking engine orchestrates high-throughput async pipelines without thread overhead, how event loops schedule tasks, and how suspending execution coordinates massive parallel workloads.
interactive_questions.explanation: In asynchronous architectures, concurrency is achieved cooperatively. Rather than relying on OS preemption (threads), a single event loop runs tasks on a single main thread. Tasks must explicitly yield control (via await) back to the scheduler, preventing idle blocks during high-latency remote database calls or network exchanges.

production_usecase.description: In a live trading environment receiving hundreds of thousands of market tick events per second across multiple exchanges, maintaining OS threads for each client session creates massive memory overhead and thread contention. Using an asynchronous asyncio scheduler allows a single loop to maintain millions of connections. Sessions suspend their execution during socket reads and yield processing power back to the global event loop to distribute ticks optimally.

glossary.definition: Concurrency model where routines voluntarily yield control to a central loop instead of being preempted by the OS.
The single-threaded coordinator that tracks active tasks, timers, and I/O status, running callbacks sequentially.
Helper that runs multiple coroutines concurrently and waits to return their combined results.
An explicit keyword that pauses a coroutine, handing execution control back to the event loop.
A block when a synchronous CPU task monopolizes the thread, halting other pending async operations.

explanation_steps.code:
# 1. Import Python's built-in cooperative asynchronous scheduling foundation library
import asyncio
# 2. Declare an asynchronous coroutine model designed to fetch a specific real-time ticket stream
async def fetch_exchange_tick(exchange_id: str):
    # 3. Print the diagnostic logging output specifying which market index is actively monitored
    print(f"Polling {exchange_id}...")
    # 4. Suspend this coroutine, returning control to the loop for 10ms of cooperative breathing room
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    # 5. Hand back the aggregated string message packet containing completed ticker transaction records
    return f"Tick data from {exchange_id}"
